business_problem: Ironclad needed to automate contract review without sacrificing control, precision, or privacy because legal teams were spending too much time on manual redlining and policy checks.
solution_summary: Ironclad embedded GPT-4 into AI Assist to automate the first pass of contract review inside its contract-lifecycle platform. The application identifies irregularities, proposes redlines, surfaces pre-approved clauses, and follows company-specific AI Playbooks so legal teams can work from their own policies rather than from generic drafting rules. Contract text enters Ironclad's editor, GPT-4 and the AI Assist workflow generate suggested changes and supporting language, and users then accept, reject, or disable those suggestions under human oversight. Ironclad also kept data-governance concerns front and center by using the API in a way that does not train OpenAI on customer-submitted data by default. That architecture makes AI a directly embedded legal-workflow feature rather than a detached assistant, which is why teams can move from manual review to governed automation in the same editor.

data_flow: Contract language enters Ironclad's editor, GPT-4 powers AI Assist to identify issues and draft redlines against AI Playbooks, and the resulting suggestions are surfaced to users who review, accept, reject, or turn off the AI output as needed.
business_outcome: Ironclad cut the time needed for an initial contract-redlining pass from forty minutes to two, accelerated adoption of AI review, and gave legal teams a governed way to work faster without removing human judgment.
